instructions: Pat the chicken thighs dry. Slice 3 thin slices of ginger and smash them with the flat of a knife. Cut 2 scallions into 3-inch pieces and smash those too.
Heat the oil in a large wide pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the ginger and cook for 30 seconds. Add the scallions and star anise and cook for 20 seconds, until you can smell them.

Pour in the 1/4 cup Shaoxing wine and let it bubble for 30 seconds. Add the 1/2 cup light soy sauce, 2 tbsp dark soy sauce, 1/3 cup sugar and 3 cups water. Stir until the sugar dissolves, then simmer on low for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, rinse the rice and cook it in 2 1/4 cups water, covered, the way you usually do.

Lay the thighs in the pot skin side up in one layer. The liquid should come about halfway up. Bring it to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook for 25 minutes. Spoon some of the liquid over the tops every 5 minutes.
Turn off the heat and leave the pot covered for 10 minutes.

You're cooking the thighs to 175°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check the thickest one there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest thigh next to the bone: the juices should run clear with no pink.
Serve the thighs over the rice with a few spoonfuls of the braising liquid spooned over.
method_notes: The Woks of Life (4.86 from 74 ratings) leads. Its whole chicken is poached in a sweet soy bath of light and dark soy, Shaoxing wine, sugar, ginger, scallion and star anise, then rests off the heat. Whole-chicken time is 1 hour 45 minutes, so this uses the leg option the page and Takes Two Eggs (thighs 40 minutes) both allow: the bath is scaled to about a quarter, and the thighs cook 25 minutes plus a 10-minute rest. The rose wine is dropped and the sugar trimmed slightly for a milder sauce. The honest time is about 55 minutes.
